title: AI Video Startup Higgsfield Valued at $5.4 Billion as Goldman Sachs and Intel Join Funding Round
excerpt: The company's annualized revenue has rocketed from zero to $500 million in 15 months, making it one of the fastest-growing AI startups in history.
body:
• AI video startup Higgsfield is in discussions to raise $300 million to $500 million at a $5.4 billion valuation, according to the Financial Times, a more than fourfold increase from its $1.3 billion valuation six months ago.
  • Goldman Sachs and Intel are among the backers joining the round, with DST Global also in discussions to participate.
  • The company has hit $500 million in annualized revenue, up from $200 million at the end of 2025, making it one of the fastest revenue ramp-ups in startup history.
  • Founded in 2023 by ex-Snap AI head Alex Mashrabov, Higgsfield has attracted over 15 million users to its AI video generation platform since launching in March 2025.

From Zero to $500 Million in 15 Months

Higgsfield AI, the San Francisco-based video generation platform, is raising between $300 million and $500 million at a valuation of approximately $5.4 billion, the Financial Times reported. The round would represent a more than fourfold increase from the $1.3 billion valuation the company achieved in January 2026 during its $80 million Series A extension.

https://x.com/AlphaWireNewsAi/status/2089247221686665707

The numbers behind the valuation jump are striking. Higgsfield crossed $500 million in annualized revenue this summer, up from $200 million at the end of 2025. The platform did not exist before March 2025, meaning it generated a half-billion-dollar revenue run rate in roughly 15 months — a trajectory that outpaces the early growth curves of companies like Slack, Zoom, and even OpenAI.

Who's Backing the Round

Goldman Sachs and Intel are joining the funding round, according to the Financial Times. DST Global, the investment firm founded by early Facebook backer Yuri Milner, has also been in discussions to participate, TechTimes reported. Previous investors include Accel, Menlo Ventures, GFT Ventures, and AI Capital Partners, who participated in earlier rounds totaling approximately $138 million.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=gpcvPA0wTqk

If the round closes at the upper end, Higgsfield would raise $500 million — roughly 3.6 times everything it has raised to date, combined. The fundraising discussions remain active and no lead investor has been publicly confirmed.

How Higgsfield Got Here

The company was founded in 2023 by Alex Mashrabov, formerly head of Generative AI at Snap, who arrived there after Snap acquired his previous startup AI Factory for $166 million in 2020. Co-founder Yerzat Dulat rounds out the founding team.

Higgsfield's browser-based platform allows users to generate, edit, and publish AI video content within a single workflow. The company does not train foundation models from scratch — instead, it post-trains and fine-tunes third-party models using proprietary data and a system it calls a "video reasoning engine" that maintains visual consistency across clips.

"We minimize the production tax so that, eventually, better stories and better ideas win."

— Alex Mashrabov, Higgsfield CEO

About 85% of activity on the platform comes from professional social media marketers, according to the company. Celebrity users including Madonna, Snoop Dogg, and Will Smith have used the platform, and brands like Qatar Airways have produced social content through it.

The AI Video Land Grab

Higgsfield's explosive growth comes as the AI video generation market undergoes rapid consolidation and competition. The company has benefited from the simultaneous exit of two of its largest rivals from the commercial video market, though it still faces competition from Runway, Synthesia, and ByteDance's expanding stack of video tools including CapCut.

Mashrabov has identified ByteDance rather than OpenAI or Adobe as Higgsfield's primary competitive benchmark, pointing to the TikTok parent company's growing suite of marketing and video creation tools. With over 15 million users and revenue growth that shows no signs of decelerating, Higgsfield is positioning itself as the platform layer that turns AI-generated video into a mainstream marketing tool.
